guidance_note: When a test pins a 'reachable kinds' set, derive each kind's membership by tracing the producer, and mutation-check both directions (remove a reachable kind's words AND add an unreachable kind's words) on both tables.

narrative: This PR turned focus from a sort into a membership scope, and every round it found more surfaces still describing the old ordering semantics or a completeness claim. The fixes were judged well (rewording over compute, deleting dead entries, mutation-verifying tests), but execution was repeatedly incomplete: the F4 claim-grep used exact phrases and missed three rewordings; each positional doc claim (first line, line above rows) was written without checking the print order; and the F6 test rewrite hand-typed a reachable set that let dead entries pass. Round 4 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings, and the PR then hit the 5-round review cap, so its final head commit went unreviewed. The round-0 summary's outside-diff findings (error_output.go remediation, readiness.go:14 and its twin) were ignored and came back as inline findings in rounds 1-3.
guidance_observations: The agent never acted on the round-0 summary's 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' list; three of those items came back later as inline threads (F11, F18, F24).
Claim sweeps searched exact multi-word phrases; searching the claim's single key word near the subject would have caught F10, F19, and F21 in the first fix.
Doc sentences written during fixes asserted output position and message content without running the command, which produced the F20->F26 and F12->F23 drift.
Tests written to catch a defect class were mutation-checked only on the side the reviewer had raised, so the symmetric vacuous case (F27) survived three rounds.
The 5-round cap ended review with fea7852 unreviewed; fix-caused rounds directly used up review capacity here.
